newsitem.title: FRANCE: CLF sees good 1996 for new group.
newsitem.headline: CLF sees good 1996 for new group.

text.p: French municipal lender Credit Local de France forecast a good 1996 for the new European banking group Dexia that it has created with Belgium's CCB.
CLF reiterated its 1996 net income would show an increase over last year and said the same would be true for Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet van Belgie.
The two banks have joined forces to create Europe's 22nd-largest banking group.

"The net income of Credit Local de France will increase in 1996 and the same will be true at Credit Communal de Belgique," the bank said. "The Dexia Group will thus report good results in its first year of existence."

Credit Local, whose annual profits have risen for nine straight years, reported first-half profits up six percent to 793 million francs ($153.4 million) and a 1995 profit of 1.48 billion francs, up two percent over the previous year.
Credit Local said total business amounted to 61 billion, representing a rise of 116 percent including Germany.
In Europe, new business as of October 31, 1996 totalled 57.3 billion francs, for an increase of 115 percent over 1995. That includes business at its German unit, CLF Hypothekenbank Berlin (HBB).
In North America, new loans and commitments rose 35 percent to 2.3 billion francs. Structured financing and project financing represented three billion francs, up 190 percent.
The two groups which specialise in financing local public authorities, signed a shareholder agreement last month sealing their alliance. The deal is retroactive to January 1, 1996.

The Dexia Group is made up of two holding companies, CLF-Dexia Farnce and Credit Communal/Dexia Belgium which jointly own the two operating subsidiaries Credit Local de France and Credit Communal de Belgique.
The new group plans to maintain its core commitment to financing of public service projects and financial services to local government authorities.
It also aims to focus on universal banking, especially in Belgium where Credit Communal is the largest customer deposit bank. In addition it is involved in private banking and asset management.
Municipally-owned Credit Communal recently floated 30 percent of its capital in Belgium's largest-ever initial public offering.
